--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.delete_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Delete an edge from the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.delete_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Delete an edge from the graph. title: >- [Graph.delete_edge()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Delete an edge from the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Delete an edge from the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L2643-L2787){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.delete_edge( source=None, target=None, id=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Delete edge](/assets/graphs/delete-edge.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Before: a four-node cycle with the edge between A and C highlighted in the accent color. After: that edge is gone, shown dashed, while all four nodes and the other three edges stay in place." width="100%"} Remove edges by specifying either the source and target nodes, or the edge ID directly. For multigraphs with source/target, only the first matching edge is deleted. Only the edge is removed; both endpoint nodes stay in the graph, even if they end up isolated. When deleting by endpoints, direction matters in a directed graph (deleting `B -> A` won't remove an `A -> B` edge), while in an undirected graph the endpoints can be given in either order. When several parallel edges connect the pair, call the method repeatedly, or use `delete_edge_by_id()` to pick a specific one. The graph is modified in place and the deletion is recorded in the step log (see `steps`). To remove many edges matching a condition, select them and use `delete_edges_ws()`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [source]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Source node ID or label. Required (together with `target=`) if `id=` is not provided. In a directed graph this must be the node the edge starts from. [target]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Union[int, str, None]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Target node ID or label. Required (together with `source=`) if `id=` is not provided. [id]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Edge ID to delete. If provided, `source=` and `target=` are ignored. Edge IDs can be found with `get_edge_ids()`, `find_edge_ids()` or the `id` column of the edge DataFrame. Default is `None`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [EdgeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If no edge exists matching the criteria (no edge between the two nodes, or no edge with the given ID). It is a subclass of both `KeyError` and `ValueError`. [NodeNotFoundError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `source=` or `target=` doesn't match any node (also a `KeyError` and a `ValueError`). [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If neither (`source`, `target`) nor `id` is provided. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Providing both `source` and `target` deletes the first matching edge between them. The nodes themselves are kept: ::: {#53f62c65 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) .delete_edge(source="A", target="B") ) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B"), graph.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (False, 3) ``` ::: ::: In a directed graph the endpoints must be given in the edge's direction. Asking for the reverse `C -> B` edge raises a `KeyError`: ::: {#1eafec8f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} try: graph.delete_edge(source="C", target="B") except KeyError as e: print(e) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` No edge found from 'C' to 'B' ``` ::: ::: When the edge ID is already known, deleting by `id=` skips the source/target lookup entirely: ::: {#4d391042 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_edge(source="A", target="B") ) edge_id = graph.get_edge_ids()[0] graph.delete_edge(id=edge_id) graph.has_edge(source="A", target="B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: With parallel edges, each call removes only one of them, so the second edge (weight `2.0`) survives: ::: {#9700cc45 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B"]) .add_edges([("A", "B", 1.0), ("A", "B", 2.0)]) .delete_edge(source="A", target="B") ) graph.get_edge_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
